what_it_is.prose: Embraer Defense & Security is the defence division of Brazilian aerospace group Embraer S.A. Its India footprint is competitive and industrial rather than operational: Embraer is offering the C-390 Millennium (military designation KC-390) twin-turbofan medium transport into the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme, in partnership with India's Mahindra Group. Embraer Defense & Security and Mahindra Defence Systems signed a Memorandum of Understanding at the Embassy of Brazil in New Delhi on 9 February 2024 to jointly pursue the MTA opportunity and develop an industrialisation plan with Indian industry. The two elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership in October 2025, and on 19 February 2026 announced a plan to establish an in-country C-390 Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) capability — spanning base and heavy maintenance, structural inspection and testing, component repair and overhaul, avionics support and training — contingent on the aircraft being selected, and positioning India as a potential regional C-390 support hub. The IAF issued the MTA Request for Proposals on 12 August 2026 for 60 aircraft (with options for more) worth roughly ₹1 lakh crore (~US$10.5 billion) in the 18-30 tonne payload class, to replace the Antonov An-32 and legacy Avro HS-748 fleets. The C-390 competes against Lockheed Martin's C-130J-30 (offered with Tata) and the Airbus A400M. The C-390 carries up to 26 tonnes, cruises at up to ~470 knots on two International Aero Engines (IAE) V2500 turbofans, and is in service with Brazil, Portugal, Hungary, the Netherlands and South Korea. As of August 2026 no Indian order, down-selection or induction has occurred.

deployments_procurement.summary: The C-390 is not in Indian service. Embraer's India footprint is as an MTA-programme contender bid with the Mahindra Group: an MoU (9 Feb 2024), a strategic partnership (Oct 2025) and a proposed in-country C-390 MRO capability (announced 19 Feb 2026). The IAF's MTA RFP (60 aircraft, ~₹1 lakh crore) was issued on 12 August 2026; no selection or order has been made.

faq.question: Is Embraer's C-390 in Indian service?
faq.answer: No. As of August 2026 the C-390 Millennium is not in Indian service and has not been ordered by the IAF. Embraer's India relevance is as a contender in the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme, bid in partnership with India's Mahindra Group. The IAF issued the MTA RFP on 12 August 2026 for 60 aircraft (~₹1 lakh crore); no selection has been made.

faq.question: What is the Embraer-Mahindra partnership?
faq.answer: Embraer Defense & Security and Mahindra Defence Systems signed an MoU at the Embassy of Brazil in New Delhi on 9 February 2024 to jointly pursue India's MTA with the C-390 and build an industrialisation plan with Indian industry. They elevated this to a strategic partnership in October 2025 and, on 19 February 2026, announced a plan to set up an in-country C-390 MRO capability (base/heavy maintenance, structural inspection, component overhaul, avionics support, training) if the aircraft is selected, positioning India as a regional C-390 support hub.
